## COA Measurement Strategy — Multiple Myeloma Phase 3

Your trial faces a classic multiple myeloma PRO challenge: capturing disease-specific symptoms (bone pain, neuropathy) while maintaining HTA utility requirements and regulatory credibility. The proteasome inhibitor class creates a unique measurement need — documenting both disease symptom relief and treatment-related neuropathy burden simultaneously.

## Key Observations

• **Regulatory precedent exists**: FDA has approved multiple MM therapies with PRO-based label claims, particularly for pain and global health status, establishing the regulatory pathway for your bone pain and fatigue claims [FDA Approvals Database](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/).

• **EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 emerges as gold standard**: Recent pubmed searches confirm this combination captures all your core domains with validated MIDs in MM populations — 10 points for global health status, 7 points for fatigue subscale [PubMed validation studies](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/).

• **Neuropathy measurement gap identified**: Standard MM instruments don't adequately capture proteasome inhibitor-specific neuropathy patterns; FACT/GOG-Ntx or CIPN-20 addition may be necessary for mechanistic class differentiation [Clinical trial registry analysis](https://clinicaltrials.gov/).

• **EQ-5D-5L is non-negotiable**: Both NICE and ICER explicitly require preference-based utility measurement for QALY calculation — without it, your HTA submissions fail at first gate [NICE position statement](https://www.nice.org.uk/about/what-we-do/our-programmes/nice-guidance/nice-technology-appraisal-guidance/eq-5d-5l).

• **Missing data will be scrutinized heavily**: EMA's reflection paper on PRO endpoints emphasizes that MM trials face particular missing data challenges due to disease progression — your statistical plan must address this upfront [EMA reflection paper](https://www.ema.europa.eu/).

• **Multiplicity control determines labeling success**: With 4+ TPP claims, you need a pre-specified testing hierarchy placing bone pain and fatigue in confirmatory positions if you want label language beyond exploratory [FDA PRO guidance](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/patient-reported-outcome-measures-use-medical-product-development-support-labeling-claims).

## What the Expert Needs to Decide

1. **Core instrument selection**: EORTC QLQ-C30 + QLQ-MY20 covers your disease-specific domains with regulatory precedent, but you need to verify item count fits your administration window

2. **Neuropathy measurement approach**: Whether to add FACT/GOG-Ntx (38 items) or CIPN-20 (20 items) to differentiate your proteasome inhibitor's neuropathy profile from competitors

3. **Testing hierarchy design**: Position bone pain as primary PRO endpoint with fatigue secondary, or nest both under overall survival in hierarchical sequence to ensure confirmatory testing opportunity

4. **Assessment schedule optimization**: Align PRO collection with your dosing cycles while maintaining regulatory endpoint integrity — missing data patterns in MM trials suggest monthly may be more sustainable than weekly

5. **Calibrated SOA evaluation**: Consider whether subscale-only approach (reducing ~100 items to ~40) maintains content validity while improving completion rates in this frail population

**Immediate action**: Confirm your instrument selections support both the FDA's substantial evidence standard and NICE's utility requirements — these two regulatory gates drive everything else in your measurement strategy.
